statement: You are given a binary tree. The tree is given as the array tree in level order, indexed from 0: the root is tree[0], and the left and right children of the node at index i are at indices 2i + 1 and 2i + 2. null marks a position with no node, and every position below a null must be null too.

Produce its preorder, inorder and postorder traversals in a single recursive walk. Each call meets its node three times: on arrival, before either child is explored (add the value to preorder); between the left and the right child (add it to inorder); and on the way out, after both children (add it to postorder).
Return all three lists: preorder, inorder and postorder.

examples.explanation: 6 has children 2 and 8, and 2 has children 1 and 4. Preorder lists each node before its subtrees.
The same walk, recording each node between its left and right subtrees. This tree is a BST, so the result is sorted.
The same walk, recording each node after both of its subtrees, so the root 6 is last.
